chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Fadalah and Safwan from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
I asked him about the man in ihram whose nails grow long. He said: 'He should not cut any of them if he can bear it; but if they hurt him, let him cut them and feed a handful of food for each nail.'

The Sheikh (may Allah have mercy on him) said: And he should not eat from the game of the land, even if someone else hunted it, whether the hunter was in ihram or not, and he should not point out the game.

key_terms.اَلْمُحْرِمِ: The pilgrim in the state of ihram

ai.seo_question: What are the rules for cutting nails and eating game for a Muslim in ihram?
ai.summary: This narration from Tahdhib al-Ahkam details the specific jurisprudence of ihram, emphasizing that nail trimming is permissible only when necessary to relieve pain, thereby balancing ritual purity with physical comfort. The requirement to feed a handful of food per nail serves as a kaffarah (expiation), reflecting the principle that minor violations of ihram restrictions incur tangible compensatory duties. Furthermore, the prohibition on consuming land game extends to all cases regardless of the hunter's status, underscoring the comprehensive nature of the sacred state's restrictions.
